# Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to use WaDorule to:

- obtain upstream inflows from USGS or CDEC gages;
- combine multiple gages;
- use user-supplied inflow data from any country;
- compute or import reservoir storage rules;
- calculate seasonal inflow weights;
- apply linear or logistic release policies; and
- save results locally.

## Complete workflow

The following script is ready to use. Edit only the section labelled
`USER SETTINGS`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
###############################################################################
# WaDorule User Workflow
#
# This script demonstrates the complete WaDorule workflow:
#
#   1. Install and load WaDorule
#   2. Select an inflow source:
#        - USGS gages
#        - CDEC gages
#        - User-provided gages
#        - International/non-US gages
#   3. Compute or import a reservoir storage rule
#   4. Calculate seasonal inflow weights
#   5. Apply a linear or logistic release policy
#   6. Save outputs locally
#   7. Create optional plots
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - Each reservoir must provide its own storage and elevation information.
# - WaDorule does not use a default reservoir elevation curve.
# - Storage used by wad_release_policy() must be in MCM.
# - Flow and release values in this example are in m3/s.
# - Elevation values in this example are in m.
###############################################################################


###############################################################################
# 1. INSTALL AND LOAD WADORULE
###############################################################################

# Install the exact released version used in the study:
#
# install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github(
#   "waswapeter/WaDorule",
#   ref = "v0.1.0",
#   upgrade = "never"
# )

library(WaDorule)

# Check the installed version
packageVersion("WaDorule")

# View exported functions
ls("package:WaDorule")

# Open function documentation if required
# ?wad_get_upstream_inflows
# ?wad_compute_target_storage
# ?wad_seasonal_weights
# ?wad_release_policy


###############################################################################
# 2. USER SETTINGS
###############################################################################

## ---- Date period ------------------------------------------------------------

start_date <- "2000-01-01"
end_date   <- "2020-12-31"


## ---- Inflow source ----------------------------------------------------------

# Select one of the following:
#
#   "usgs"
#   "cdec"
#   "user"
#   "international"
#   "combined"
#
inflow_source <- "usgs"


## ---- USGS settings ----------------------------------------------------------

# Enter one or more USGS site numbers.
#
# Example:
# usgs_sites <- c("02087183", "02087275")

usgs_sites <- c("02087183")


## ---- CDEC settings ----------------------------------------------------------

# CDEC requires the optional CDECRetrieve package.
#
# Install it once if needed:
#
# install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("FlowWest/CDECRetrieve")

# Enter one or more CDEC station codes.
cdec_sites <- c("ISB")

# CDEC sensor and duration code
cdec_sensor   <- "76"
cdec_dur_code <- "D"

# Confirm the units returned by the selected CDEC sensor.
# Sensor 76 is commonly reported in cfs, but users should verify this.
cdec_units <- "cfs"


## ---- User-provided inflow settings -----------------------------------------

# For user-provided inflows, the data frame must contain:
#
#   Date
#   one or more flow columns
#
# Example:
#
# user_inflows <- data.frame(
#   Date = as.Date(c("2000-01-01", "2000-01-02")),
#   Gage_A = c(100, 125),
#   Gage_B = c(50, 75)
# )
#
# Set user_flow_cols to the names of the columns that should be summed.
#
# If user_flow_cols = NULL, all numeric columns except Date are used.

user_inflows <- NULL
user_flow_cols <- NULL

# Example for reading a user file:
#
# user_inflows <- read.csv(
#   "C:/path/to/user_inflows.csv",
#   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
# )
#
# user_inflows$Date <- as.Date(
#   user_inflows$Date,
#   format = "%Y-%m-%d"
# )
#
# user_flow_cols <- c("Gage_A", "Gage_B")

user_inflow_units <- "cfs"


## ---- International/non-US inflow settings -----------------------------------

# International or non-US data can be supplied in exactly the same format:
#
#   Date
#   one or more flow columns
#
# Example:
#
# international_inflows <- read.csv(
#   "C:/path/to/international_gages.csv",
#   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
# )
#
# international_inflows$Date <- as.Date(
#   international_inflows$Date,
#   format = "%Y-%m-%d"
# )
#
# international_flow_cols <- c("Gage_001", "Gage_002")

international_inflows <- NULL
international_flow_cols <- NULL
international_units <- "m3s"

# Optional non-US site identifiers and custom reader.
#
# A custom reader must accept:
#
#   site
#   start_date
#   end_date
#
# and return a data frame containing Date and one or more flow columns.

international_sites <- NULL
international_reader <- NULL

# Example custom reader:
#
# international_reader <- function(site, start_date, end_date) {
#
#   file_name <- paste0(site, "_daily_flow.csv")
#
#   x <- read.csv(
#     file_name,
#     stringsAsFactors = FALSE
#   )
#
#   x$Date <- as.Date(x$Date)
#
#   x[
#     x$Date >= start_date &
#       x$Date <= end_date,
#     ,
#     drop = FALSE
#   ]
# }


## ---- Flow units -------------------------------------------------------------

# Final inflow units returned by WaDorule:
#
#   "m3s" = cubic metres per second
#   "cfs" = cubic feet per second

inflow_output_units <- "m3s"


## ---- Missing-data behavior --------------------------------------------------

# TRUE:
#   Missing values are ignored when summing multiple gages.
#
# FALSE:
#   A missing value from any contributing source produces NA for that date.

na_rm <- TRUE


###############################################################################
# 3. DOWNLOAD OR IMPORT UPSTREAM INFLOWS
###############################################################################

if (!inflow_source %in% c(
  "usgs",
  "cdec",
  "user",
  "international",
  "combined"
)) {
  stop(
    "inflow_source must be one of: ",
    paste(
      c("usgs", "cdec", "user", "international", "combined"),
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

## ---- USGS inflows -----------------------------------------------------------

if (inflow_source == "usgs") {

  qin <- wad_get_upstream_inflows(
    usgs_sites = usgs_sites,
    start_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    units = inflow_output_units,
    na_rm = na_rm
  )
}


## ---- CDEC inflows -----------------------------------------------------------

if (inflow_source == "cdec") {

  qin <- wad_get_upstream_inflows(
    cdec_sites = cdec_sites,
    cdec_sensor = cdec_sensor,
    cdec_dur_code = cdec_dur_code,
    cdec_units = cdec_units,
    start_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    units = inflow_output_units,
    na_rm = na_rm
  )
}


## ---- User-provided inflows --------------------------------------------------

if (inflow_source == "user") {

  if (is.null(user_inflows)) {
    stop(
      "Set user_inflows to a data frame or read a user inflow CSV file."
    )
  }

  qin <- wad_get_upstream_inflows(
    inflow_data = user_inflows,
    user_flow_cols = user_flow_cols,
    inflow_units = user_inflow_units,
    start_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    units = inflow_output_units,
    na_rm = na_rm
  )
}


## ---- International/non-US inflows -------------------------------------------

if (inflow_source == "international") {

  if (is.null(international_inflows) &&
      is.null(international_reader)) {
    stop(
      "Provide international_inflows or international_reader."
    )
  }

  qin <- wad_get_upstream_inflows(
    other_data = international_inflows,
    other_flow_cols = international_flow_cols,
    other_units = international_units,
    other_sites = international_sites,
    other_reader = international_reader,
    start_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    units = inflow_output_units,
    na_rm = na_rm
  )
}


## ---- Combined sources -------------------------------------------------------

# This option can combine USGS, CDEC, user-provided, and international data.
#
# Before selecting "combined", define the required objects above.

if (inflow_source == "combined") {

  qin <- wad_get_upstream_inflows(
    usgs_sites = usgs_sites,
    cdec_sites = cdec_sites,
    cdec_sensor = cdec_sensor,
    cdec_dur_code = cdec_dur_code,
    cdec_units = cdec_units,
    inflow_data = user_inflows,
    user_flow_cols = user_flow_cols,
    inflow_units = user_inflow_units,
    other_data = international_inflows,
    other_flow_cols = international_flow_cols,
    other_units = international_units,
    other_sites = international_sites,
    other_reader = international_reader,
    start_date = start_date,
    end_date = end_date,
    units = inflow_output_units,
    na_rm = na_rm
  )
}


## ---- Inspect inflows --------------------------------------------------------

if (!all(c("Date", "Q_upstream") %in% names(qin))) {
  stop(
    "The inflow output must contain Date and Q_upstream columns."
  )
}

head(qin)
summary(qin$Q_upstream)


###############################################################################
# 4. COMPUTE SEASONAL INFLOW WEIGHTS
###############################################################################

# The inflow record should ideally contain all 12 calendar months.
#
# Seasonal weights are normalized so that their average is approximately 1.
# A value greater than 1 indicates above-average monthly inflow.
# A value less than 1 indicates below-average monthly inflow.

seasonal_weights <- wad_seasonal_weights(
  inflow_df = qin,
  inflow_col = "Q_upstream",
  missing_month = "error",
  na_rm = TRUE
)

print(seasonal_weights)

# Confirm normalization
mean(seasonal_weights)


###############################################################################
# 5. USER STORAGE-RULE SETTINGS
###############################################################################

# Select one:
#
#   "direct_storage"
#       The input file already contains a storage rule.
#
#   "elevation_only"
#       The input contains elevation, and storage is calculated from
#       user-supplied elevation and storage limits.
#
storage_rule_source <- "direct_storage"


## ---- Storage-rule file ------------------------------------------------------

# Each reservoir must provide its own storage or elevation data.
# WaDorule does not use a universal default reservoir curve.

storage_rule_file <- "C:/path/to/your/storage_rule.csv"


## ---- Storage units and operational limits -----------------------------------

# These values are required only when storage is calculated from elevation.

min_storage_acft <- 10000
max_storage_acft <- 50000

# Optional operational elevation limits in feet.
# If NULL, the minimum and maximum elevations in the input data are used.

min_elev_ft <- NULL
max_elev_ft <- NULL


###############################################################################
# 6. COMPUTE OR IMPORT THE STORAGE RULE
###############################################################################

if (!storage_rule_source %in% c(
  "direct_storage",
  "elevation_only"
)) {
  stop(
    "storage_rule_source must be 'direct_storage' or 'elevation_only'."
  )
}

if (!file.exists(storage_rule_file)) {
  stop(
    "Storage-rule file was not found: ",
    storage_rule_file
  )
}

if (storage_rule_source == "direct_storage") {

  # The file must contain a recognized storage column, such as:
  #
  #   target_storage_MCM
  #   Target_Storage_MCM
  #   storage_MCM
  #   target_storage_acft
  #   Storage
  #
  # If storage is supplied directly, minimum and maximum storage limits are
  # not required for this function.

  target_storage <- wad_compute_target_storage(
    elev_file = storage_rule_file
  )
}

if (storage_rule_source == "elevation_only") {

  # The file must contain an elevation column such as Target_Elev or Elevation.
  # Storage is calculated from user-supplied operational limits.

  target_storage <- wad_compute_target_storage(
    elev_file = storage_rule_file,
    min_storage_acft = min_storage_acft,
    max_storage_acft = max_storage_acft,
    min_elev_ft = min_elev_ft,
    max_elev_ft = max_elev_ft
  )
}

head(target_storage)


###############################################################################
# 7. PROVIDE DAILY RESERVOIR STORAGE FOR THE RELEASE POLICY
###############################################################################

# wad_release_policy() requires a data frame with:
#
#   Date
#   Storage
#
# Storage must be the actual daily reservoir storage state used to determine
# releases, expressed in MCM.
#
# This may be:
#
#   - observed daily storage,
#   - simulated daily storage,
#   - or another daily operational storage series.
#
# The target storage rule calculated above is an operational target. It is not
# automatically used as the current storage state.

storage_state_file <- "C:/path/to/your/daily_reservoir_storage.csv"

if (!file.exists(storage_state_file)) {
  stop(
    "Daily reservoir storage file was not found: ",
    storage_state_file
  )
}

storage_state <- utils::read.csv(
  storage_state_file,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if (!"Date" %in% names(storage_state)) {
  stop("The storage-state file must contain a Date column.")
}

if (!"Storage" %in% names(storage_state)) {
  stop(
    "The storage-state file must contain a Storage column in MCM."
  )
}

storage_state$Date <- as.Date(storage_state$Date)

if (anyNA(storage_state$Date)) {
  stop("The storage-state file contains invalid dates.")
}

storage_state$Storage <- as.numeric(storage_state$Storage)

if (all(is.na(storage_state$Storage))) {
  stop("The Storage column contains no valid numeric values.")
}

storage_state <- storage_state[
  storage_state$Date >= as.Date(start_date) &
    storage_state$Date <= as.Date(end_date),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (nrow(storage_state) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No daily storage data are available for the selected date range."
  )
}


###############################################################################
# 8. SELECT RELEASE-POLICY SETTINGS
###############################################################################

# Select either:
#
#   "linear"
#   "logistic"
#
release_rule <- "logistic"

# Release limits in m3/s
Qmin <- 0.57
Qmax <- 550

# Storage limits in MCM
#
# These values should correspond to the reservoir's operational storage range.
Smin <- 0.5
Smax <- 200.12

# Logistic parameters are used only when release_rule = "logistic".
logistic_k <- 8
logistic_midpoint <- 0.55

# Normalize the seasonal weights so their mean is 1.
normalize_weights <- TRUE

# If TRUE, final releases are constrained between Qmin and Qmax.
cap_release <- TRUE


###############################################################################
# 9. GENERATE DAILY RELEASES
###############################################################################

release_df <- wad_release_policy(
  df = storage_state,
  seasonal_weights = seasonal_weights,
  Smin = Smin,
  Smax = Smax,
  Qmin = Qmin,
  Qmax = Qmax,
  rule = release_rule,
  logistic_k = logistic_k,
  logistic_midpoint = logistic_midpoint,
  normalize_weights = normalize_weights,
  missing_weight = 1,
  cap_release = cap_release,
  plot = FALSE
)

head(release_df)
summary(release_df$Release)


###############################################################################
# 10. OPTIONAL: COMPARE LINEAR AND LOGISTIC POLICIES
###############################################################################

release_linear <- wad_release_policy(
  df = storage_state,
  seasonal_weights = seasonal_weights,
  Smin = Smin,
  Smax = Smax,
  Qmin = Qmin,
  Qmax = Qmax,
  rule = "linear",
  normalize_weights = normalize_weights,
  cap_release = cap_release,
  plot = FALSE
)

release_logistic <- wad_release_policy(
  df = storage_state,
  seasonal_weights = seasonal_weights,
  Smin = Smin,
  Smax = Smax,
  Qmin = Qmin,
  Qmax = Qmax,
  rule = "logistic",
  logistic_k = logistic_k,
  logistic_midpoint = logistic_midpoint,
  normalize_weights = normalize_weights,
  cap_release = cap_release,
  plot = FALSE
)


###############################################################################
# 11. SAVE RESULTS LOCALLY
###############################################################################

# Users can choose any local directory.
# The default below creates an output folder in the current working directory.

output_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "output")

if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(
    output_dir,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )
}

utils::write.csv(
  qin,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "upstream_inflows.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  data.frame(
    Month = names(seasonal_weights),
    Seasonal_Weight = as.numeric(seasonal_weights)
  ),
  file = file.path(output_dir, "seasonal_weights.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  target_storage,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "target_storage_rule.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  storage_state,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "daily_storage_state.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  release_df,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "release_policy.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  release_linear,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "release_policy_linear.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  release_logistic,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "release_policy_logistic.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

message(
  "Results saved to: ",
  normalizePath(output_dir, winslash = "/")
)


###############################################################################
# 12. OPTIONAL PLOTS
###############################################################################

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {

  inflow_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    qin,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Q_upstream
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      color = "steelblue",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Aggregated Upstream Inflows",
      x = "Date",
      y = paste0("Inflow (", inflow_output_units, ")")
    )

  storage_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    storage_state,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Storage
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      color = "darkgreen",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = Smin,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "red"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = Smax,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "red"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Daily Reservoir Storage",
      x = "Date",
      y = "Storage (MCM)"
    )

  release_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    release_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Release
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      color = "firebrick",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = paste(
        "Daily Reservoir Release Policy -",
        release_rule
      ),
      x = "Date",
      y = "Release (m3/s)"
    )

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(output_dir, "upstream_inflows.png"),
    plot = inflow_plot,
    width = 8,
    height = 5,
    dpi = 300
  )

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(output_dir, "daily_storage.png"),
    plot = storage_plot,
    width = 8,
    height = 5,
    dpi = 300
  )

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(output_dir, "release_policy.png"),
    plot = release_plot,
    width = 8,
    height = 5,
    dpi = 300
  )

  print(inflow_plot)
  print(storage_plot)
  print(release_plot)

} else {
  message(
    "ggplot2 is not installed. CSV files were saved, but plots were skipped."
  )
}


###############################################################################
# END OF WADORULE WORKFLOW
###############################################################################
```^X
